participantInstructions: You and your teammate will read the Performance Indicators and the situation for this event, which is presented as a case study. You will have 30 minutes to review the case, discuss the performance indicators, and prepare your presentation. You will then have up to 15 minutes to present your recommendation to the judge and to respond to the judge's questions. Both members of the participant team must take part in presenting and in answering the judge. You will be evaluated on how well each performance indicator is demonstrated. Turn in all of your notes and materials to the judge when you finish.
situation:
You are the client relations manager and the operations manager at HALLOWAY STAFFING SOLUTIONS, a regional staffing agency now run by its third generation of family ownership. The owner (judge) has called the two of you into her office to work through a problem that has been quietly building for months. Business background is the same throughout: Halloway places temporary and contract associates with client businesses across the region, and its name rests on sending associates who are genuinely ready to work.

Halloway's largest account is Bayview Resort & Spa, a hospitality client whose contract requires every associate placed in a guest-facing role to first complete Halloway's compliance training, a program covering workplace conduct, guest-recovery conversations, and basic hospitality standards. Bayview credits that requirement for Halloway's edge over larger, less specialized staffing competitors, and renewed its contract last year partly on that promise. At the same time, Halloway's placement agreement with its registered associates guarantees a shift within forty-eight hours of a completed application, a guarantee built into every recruiting flyer the agency has printed for a decade.

The compliance training runs only twice a month across three sessions, so almost no newly registered associate can finish it before the forty-eight-hour window closes. For months, coordinators have handled the conflict by sending associates to Bayview shifts right away and telling them to finish training afterward, and afterward rarely comes. Bayview's front-desk manager recently asked why several associates could not answer routine guest-complaint questions, while two registered associates separately told the operations manager that holding their first paycheck until training was finished would leave them short on rent.

The owner (judge) wants a recommendation on how Halloway should handle placements to Bayview, and to any client whose contract carries the same training requirement, given that the forty-eight-hour dispatch guarantee cannot be met on a training schedule that runs longer than two days. She wants to know whether the agency should hold associates back until training is complete, keep placing them on the current schedule and rebuild the training around it, or handle the two obligations some other defensible way, and what each choice would cost.

Holding associates back would protect the training requirement Bayview pays for, but it would break the dispatch guarantee that drew many associates to Halloway over competing agencies in the first place, and could push them toward agencies with fewer strings attached. Continuing to place associates first preserves that guarantee and keeps shifts filled, but leaves Bayview relying on staff who have not been trained to the standard its contract specifies, risking the account Halloway has held the longest.

The owner (judge) will greet the client relations manager and the operations manager, and will ask to hear their recommendation for handling the training conflict going forward. After the presentation and questions, she will thank the participants for their work. She is not looking for a script, only a workable path she can put in place before the next hiring cycle begins.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of HALLOWAY STAFFING SOLUTIONS, a regional staffing agency now in its third generation of family ownership. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have asked the client relations manager and the operations manager to recommend how the agency should handle placements to Bayview Resort & Spa, and to any client whose contract carries the same compliance-training requirement, given that the forty-eight-hour dispatch guarantee to associates cannot be met on a training schedule that runs longer than two days. You want to hear whether they recommend holding associates back until training is complete, continuing the current placement schedule and rebuilding training around it, or another defensible path, and you want to understand what each choice would cost the agency, the client, and the associates.

During the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What would you say to an associate who is asked to wait for a paycheck until training is finished?
What would you say to Bayview's front-desk manager the next time an untrained associate is on a shift?
